title: HTTP/JSON vs gRPC vs service mesh
description: Protocol and proxy placement. TLS/mTLS is identity on the wire, not authorization of money.

cells.workload: Public and service APIs, caches, browsers, idempotent GETs.
cells.consistency: HTTP semantics do not create a consistency model. POST retries need keys.
cells.latency: JSON encode plus TLS. HTTP/2 multiplexing helps; head-of-line still exists at the app.
cells.scaling: Stateless handlers. CDN can cache GETs only.
cells.failure: 4xx vs 5xx vs timeout. 429 needs a Retry-After you honor.
cells.costOps: Easy to observe. Schema drift is a product problem.
cells.whenNot: Tight streaming fan-in where protobuf + HTTP/2 streams are the budget, or treating 200 as commit.

cells.workload: Service-to-service RPCs, streaming, deadlines as first-class.
cells.consistency: Deadlines abort the RPC, not the server-side commit.
cells.latency: Protobuf + HTTP/2. Tail from server processing, not JSON.
cells.scaling: Client load-balancing policies. Long streams pin memory.
cells.failure: UNAVAILABLE vs DEADLINE_EXCEEDED vs UNKNOWN. Retries need idempotency.
cells.costOps: Codegen, deadline propagation, and debug with traces not curl-only.
cells.whenNot: Browser-first public APIs without a gateway, or unbounded bidirectional streams as a queue.

cells.workload: mTLS, retries, outlier detection, telemetry around existing apps.
cells.consistency: Retry policies can duplicate non-idempotent writes. Outlier ejection is membership, not fencing.
cells.latency: Extra hop per sidecar. Warm connections help; cold start hurts.
cells.scaling: Sidecar CPU/RAM per pod. Control plane push lag.
cells.failure: Sidecar crash blackholes the pod. Control plane loss freezes config.
cells.costOps: Highest ops burden of the three. Cert rotation and retry storms.
cells.whenNot: A gateway plus library retries would have been enough, or auto-retry of TokenX POSTs.

assumptions: mTLS does not replace application authorization.
Mesh sidecar outage is an independent failure from the app process.
